Start or resume playing the audio stream.

detaileddescription.para: This function starts the stream if it was stopped, resumes it if it was paused, and restarts it from the beginning if it was already playing. This function uses its own thread so that it doesn't block the rest of the program while the stream is played.

briefdescription.para: Pause the audio stream.

detaileddescription.para: This function pauses the stream if it was playing, otherwise (stream already paused or stopped) it has no effect.

briefdescription.para: Stop playing the audio stream.

detaileddescription.para: This function stops the stream if it was playing or paused, and does nothing if it was already stopped. It also resets the playing position (unlike pause()).

briefdescription.para: Return the number of channels of the stream.

detaileddescription.para: 1 channel means a mono sound, 2 means stereo, etc.

briefdescription.para: Get the stream sample rate of the stream.

detaileddescription.para: The sample rate is the number of audio samples played per second. The higher, the better the quality.

simplesect.para: Sample rate, in number of samples per second

briefdescription.para: Get the map of position in sample frame to sound channel.

detaileddescription.para: This is used to map a sample in the sample stream to a position during spatialization.

simplesect.para: Map of position in sample frame to sound channel

briefdescription.para: Get the current status of the stream (stopped, paused, playing)
Change the current playing position of the stream.

detaileddescription.para: The playing position can be changed when the stream is either paused or playing. Changing the playing position when the stream is stopped has no effect, since playing the stream would reset its position.

parameterdescription.para: New playing position, from the beginning of the stream

briefdescription.para: Get the current playing position of the stream.

simplesect.para: Current playing position, from the beginning of the stream

briefdescription.para: Set whether or not the stream should loop after reaching the end.

detaileddescription.para: If set, the stream will restart from beginning after reaching the end and so on, until it is stopped or setLooping(false) is called. The default looping state for streams is false.

parameterdescription.para: true to play in loop, false to play once

briefdescription.para: Tell whether or not the stream is in loop mode.

simplesect.para: true if the stream is looping, false otherwise

briefdescription.para: Set the effect processor to be applied to the sound.

detaileddescription.para: The effect processor is a callable that will be called with sound data to be processed.

parameterdescription.para: The effect processor to attach to this sound, attach an empty processor to disable processing

briefdescription.para: Define the audio stream parameters.

detaileddescription.para: This function must be called by derived classes as soon as they know the audio settings of the stream to play. Any attempt to manipulate the stream (play(), ...) before calling this function will fail. It can be called multiple times if the settings of the audio stream change, but only when the stream is stopped.

parameterdescription.para: Number of channels of the stream
Sample rate, in samples per second

briefdescription.para: Request a new chunk of audio samples from the stream source.

detaileddescription.para: This function must be overridden by derived classes to provide the audio samples to play. It is called continuously by the streaming loop, in a separate thread. The source can choose to stop the streaming loop at any time, by returning false to the caller. If you return true (i.e. continue streaming) it is important that the returned array of samples is not empty; this would stop the stream due to an internal limitation.

simplesect.para: true to continue playback, false to stop

briefdescription.para: Change the current playing position in the stream source.

detaileddescription.para: This function must be overridden by derived classes to allow random seeking into the stream source.

parameterdescription.para: New playing position, relative to the beginning of the stream

briefdescription.para: Change the current playing position in the stream source to the beginning of the loop.

detaileddescription.para: This function can be overridden by derived classes to allow implementation of custom loop points. Otherwise, it just calls onSeek(Time::Zero) and returns 0.

simplesect.para: The seek position after looping (or std::nullopt if there's no loop)

briefdescription.para: Get the sound object.
Abstract base class for streamed audio sources.

detaileddescription.para: Unlike audio buffers (see sf::SoundBuffer), audio streams are never completely loaded in memory. Instead, the audio data is acquired continuously while the stream is playing. This behavior allows to play a sound with no loading delay, and keeps the memory consumption very low.

Sound sources that need to be streamed are usually big files (compressed audio musics that would eat hundreds of MB in memory) or files that would take a lot of time to be received (sounds played over the network).

sf::SoundStream is a base class that doesn't care about the stream source, which is left to the derived class. SFML provides a built-in specialization for big files (see sf::Music). No network stream source is provided, but you can write your own by combining this class with the network module.

A derived class has to override two virtual functions:
onGetData fills a new chunk of audio data to be played
onSeek changes the current playing position in the source
It is important to note that each SoundStream is played in its own separate thread, so that the streaming loop doesn't block the rest of the program. In particular, the onGetData and onSeek virtual functions may sometimes be called from this separate thread. It is important to keep this in mind, because you may have to take care of synchronization issues if you share data between threads.
